deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these 1974 'topologie modérée' notes, the previous page draws a 2-dimensional stratified space with a point stratum V_0, a curve stratum V_1 and an open stratum V_2. It also draws the boundary pieces of the tubular neighbourhoods: V_21 is the edge of V_2 along V_1, V_20 is the edge of V_2 around V_0, and V_210 is the corner where they meet. The next page builds stratified spaces by successive gluing (manifolds with boundary, fibred boundaries, mapping-cylinder-type collapse). This page is the bridge between the two: it encodes a 2-dimensional tame stratified space, and objects living on it, as a diagram of compact manifolds with corners plus fibrations of boundary faces over lower strata.

(1) Geometric data (left and right middle diagrams).
- Φ_0 is the 0-dimensional stratum, a finite set.
- Φ_1 is the closed 1-stratum with its tubular neighbourhood of Φ_0 removed. It is a compact 1-manifold with boundary ∂Φ_1, which comes with an inclusion into Φ_1 and a projection π̄_1: ∂Φ_1 → Φ_0.
- Φ_2 is the 2-stratum with tubes removed. It is a compact surface with corners.
- Its boundary ∂Φ_2 decomposes into two faces:
  - ∂_0Φ_2, the arcs around the points, which fibre via (π_2)_0 over Φ_0;
  - ∂_1Φ_2, the arcs parallel to the curves.
- The face ∂_1Φ_2 is itself a 1-dimensional stratified object:
  - its 0-part (∂_1Φ_2)_0 maps to Φ_0;
  - its 1-part (∂_1Φ_2)_1 maps by π_{2,1,1} (a finite covering) to Φ_1;
  - its boundary ∂(∂_1Φ_2)_1 (the corners) maps by ∂π_{2,1,1} to ∂Φ_1, compatibly with π̄_1.
- The maps α_0, α_1 (face inclusions) and β_0, β_1 (corner inclusions) record the corner structure.
- The tower X_0 = Φ_0 ⊂ X_1 ⊂ X_2 is recovered by gluing. Each Φ_i is attached along its boundary to X_{i-1} through these projections, i.e. a mapping-cylinder collapse of the tubes. This is exactly the procedure written out on the next page.
- Grothendieck notes that the boundary data (Ψ_0, Ψ_1) is again a lower-dimensional object of the same type. The description is therefore recursive: the boundary of the top piece is a stratified space of one dimension less, fibred over the lower strata.

(2) Coefficient data (top line).
- F_0, F_1, F_2 are objects attached to Φ_0, Φ_1, Φ_2, with ∂F_i := F_i|∂Φ_i.
- A map φ relates F_0 to ∂F_1 (drawn as an arrow from F_0 up to ∂F_1, i.e. π̄_1^*F_0 → F_1|∂Φ_1).
- For F_2 there are restrictions to the faces ∂_0F_2 and ∂_1F_2 = (∂_1F_2)_0, (∂_1F_2)_1, linked by arrows α, β compatible on corners.
- Most plausibly F_i are locally constant sheaves (or fibre data) on the closed pieces. The φ, α, β are then specialisation/gluing maps from deeper strata to shallower ones.
- If so, this is a gluing description of constructible sheaves (or stratified fibrations) on X: local systems on each piece Φ_i, plus specialisation maps on boundary faces, plus coherence on corners. In modern terms, that is a representation of the exit-path category, presented via the 'unzipped' manifolds with corners.

(3) Combinatorial / algebraic classification (bottom).
- Φ_0 is a finite set.
- Φ_1 = {Φ_1°, Φ_1^b} splits into closed components (circles) and components with boundary (segments).
- Each component is classified by a Z/2Z-torsor ('cercles orientés ordinaires': the orientations, or the two endpoints).
- The arrow back to Φ_0 records where segment endpoints go.
- Φ_2 = {F →i G} is encoded algebraically:
  - a 'prégroupoïde 1-spécial' F, the boundary data;
  - a 'groupoïde 2-spécial' G, presumably the fundamental groupoid of the surface with its peripheral structure;
  - 'foncteurs admissibles' as the maps.
- The constraint ∂_0Φ_2 ⊂ π_0 F says the vertex-type boundary arcs are among the components of the boundary data.
- Likewise Ψ_0 is a finite set and Ψ_1 = {Ψ_1°, Ψ_1^b} for the boundary structure.
- So the page aims at a purely algebraic description of 2-dimensional tame stratified spaces up to isotopy:
  - finite sets and Z/2-torsors for dimensions 0 and 1;
  - surfaces with boundary through fundamental groupoids with peripheral data (Dehn–Nielsen–Baer type full faithfulness).
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the page is schematic and incomplete.
The data are not stated precisely: the exact definitions of 'prégroupoïde 1-spécial', 'groupoïde 2-spécial' and 'foncteurs admissibles' are not given.

A groupoid description of a surface determines it only up to isotopy or homotopy. Faithfulness requires the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer/peripheral conditions, and it fails for the sphere, disc and annulus cases unless these are handled separately; the page does not address this.
The nature of F_i (sheaves vs. spaces) is not specified.

ideas.what: Decomposition of a stratified space into compact manifolds with corners Φ_i whose boundary faces fibre over lower strata, recursively; reconstruction by gluing / mapping cylinders.
ideas.modern_name: Thom–Mather control data / abstract stratified sets; manifolds with fibred corners (iterated fibration structures); 'unzipping' / resolution of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970), Verona (1984); Melrose; Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 on tame topology and 'dévissage' of stratified structures (only programmatic, without details)

ideas.what: Coefficient data F_i on the pieces Φ_i with restriction to boundary faces and gluing maps φ, α, β compatible on corners, i.e. constructible sheaves or stratified bundles described by data on the resolved pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Constructible sheaves as representations of the exit-path category; gluing descriptions of perverse/constructible sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished); Treumann (2009); Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); MacPherson–Vilonen (gluing)

ideas.what: Classification of compact 1-manifolds and of 1-strata data by finite sets with Z/2Z-torsors (orientations/endpoints).

Encoding compact surfaces with boundary by algebraic groupoid data (a 2-special groupoid with peripheral 1-special pregroupoid and admissible functors), so that 2-dimensional tame stratified spaces become equivalent to purely algebraic data.
ideas.modern_name: Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem / 'anabelian' nature of surfaces; peripheral group systems; fundamental groupoids with base points on boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn, Nielsen, Baer (1920s); Zieschang–Vogt–Coldewey for groupoid/peripheral versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to discrete/profinite fundamental groupoids of surfaces describing their topology (Teichmüller tower), but not this stratified version

missed.claim: Grothendieck combines a resolution-by-manifolds-with-corners description of tame stratified spaces with an algebraic (groupoid/torsor) encoding of each piece. The aim is a purely algebraic model of the category of 2-dimensional tame stratified spaces, i.e. a 'stratified Dehn–Nielsen–Baer' theorem linking tame topology to his anabelian/groupoid viewpoint. The literature treats unzipping/exit paths and surface-group rigidity separately; an explicit algebraic classification of 2-dimensional stratified spaces via such data does not appear to be standard.
missed.quote: Φ_2 = { F →i G } ... prégroupoïde 1-spécial, groupoïde 2-spécial, foncteurs admissibles; ∂_0Φ_2 ⊂ π_0 F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give a combinatorial/algebraic model of 2-dimensional stratified spaces and of their mapping class groupoids. This is relevant to Esquisse-type Teichmüller towers on singular surfaces and to factorization homology on 2-dimensional stratified spaces.

missed.claim: The data F_i with boundary restrictions and gluing maps φ, α_i, β_i on the corner diagram sketch an exit-path / unzipping description of constructible coefficients on a stratified space, about 15–35 years before MacPherson, Treumann and Lurie. It is left as a diagram without a theorem.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical priority: an early form of the exit-path description of constructible sheaves via resolved strata (as in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It is not new mathematics today.

deep.surprise_reason: The resolution/unzipping picture itself is known (Thom–Mather, Esquisse). Two features are less expected for 1974: the apparent gluing description of coefficient data, anticipating exit-path ideas, and the attempt to encode 2-dimensional stratified spaces purely algebraically via special groupoids. The notation is too sketchy to claim a finished result.
